the_defect.what: --repair-boundary repairs the partial bar the PREVIOUS run left behind; it cannot help the one the CURRENT run creates. The fetch asks for 'now', IBKR answers with the minute in progress, and the append stores that snapshot as a finished bar.
the_defect.evidence: Stage 5Q-7, 2026-08-24: the approved repair fixed the 13:45 bars in MNQ/MYM/M2K and the same run left new partial bars at 20:20 and 20:21; the re-probe returned repairable_dry_run instead of nothing_to_repair
the_defect.conclusion: repairing moves the defect one minute later; only refusing to store it removes it

the_fix.rule: a bar stamped T covers [T, T+1min), so it is complete exactly when the observation instant has reached T + BAR_SECONDS (60)

clock.why: the snapshot IBKR answers with is at or after the moment we asked; stamping afterwards would let a minute that closed during the round trip look complete while the row held for it is still the partial one
clock.cost: at most one just-closed minute deferred to the next run, which appends it as an ordinary new bar
clock.pinned_by: an AST test requiring the stamp to precede the request
